nodes.xbox-launch.summary.en.text: Paid media for Genshin Impact’s Xbox launch had to drive console players to the landing page. I led the creative strategy across the US, France and Germany: four testable concepts, localised for each market, read with the media strategist to see which won where and scale it.

nodes.ua-creative-strategy.summary.en.text: The Genshin Impact brand team had creators and production budget; the paid acquisition team needed more creator ads that converted. I built the pipeline between them from scratch: aligned both teams on the metrics that mattered, turned those into a creative testing framework, and scaled the formats that brought in higher-value users across Japan, North America and Europe.

nodes.ua-creative-strategy.sections.0.it.text: The acquisition team's tests showed creator ads scaled and converted well, but they couldn't produce enough of them. The brand team had creator resources but had never worked on user acquisition.

nodes.zzz-jp-accounts.summary.en.text: Zenless Zone Zero was new in Japan and needed social channels that reached players beyond its official accounts. I took the first few channels from launch to a nine-channel network: worked out which positions and formats Japanese players responded to, cut what didn’t work, and turned the rest into a system the ZZZ team now runs.

nodes.ua-creative-strategy.team.en.text: Me (creative strategy, brand team), 1 acquisition strategist, 1 acquisition specialist and 4 agency partners. The acquisition team owned media buying and budget; I owned creative strategy and production.

nodes.zzz-jp-accounts.team.en.text: Me (social strategy), 2 content reviewers and 3 agency partners

nodes.ua-creative-strategy.sections.0.it.text: I had to build the pipeline from scratch and prove, within a few game updates, that our creative could earn spend and bring in quality users, not just add volume. The budget only covered smaller creators, so the content itself had to do the work.

nodes.gip-testing.summary.en.text: TikTok’s Gaming Incentive Programme pays creators to post about a game. Could it bring in users for Genshin Impact at acquisition-level efficiency, and could its videos work as ads? I designed a three-round test to answer both, each round measured against our acquisition benchmarks. The reach was efficient; the users and the content weren’t strong enough to scale, so I recommended stopping the programme and moving the budget to creator ads.

nodes.xbox-launch.team.en.text: Me (creative strategy), 1 media strategist, 2 creative producers and 1 agency partner

nodes.influencer-activation.summary.en.text: For a flagship Genshin Impact character launch on X, I refreshed the creator strategy: a lineup built around the creators core players actually follow, pointed at the official event and its reward codes.

nodes.genshin-en-accounts.summary.en.text: For Genshin Impact’s eight creator-style English-language channels on TikTok and YouTube, grown organically, I diagnosed why the established ones had stalled, refreshed their content mix, and set the strategy for the new ones from scratch.

nodes.giveaway-campaign.summary.en.text: For a major Genshin Impact update, I led a giveaway hosted by the biggest Genshin fan account on X and seeded by 67 creators across X, TikTok and Instagram.

nodes.interactive-filter.summary.en.text: For Genshin Impact’s Lunar New Year event, I shaped two AR filters for TikTok and Snapchat that were fun and easy for anyone to join in, and briefed 70+ creators to set the trend off in the first week.

nodes.landing-page.summary.en.text: For a major Genshin Impact update, I designed the mechanic that turned the launch landing page into a game: a short personality quiz with a shareable result, and a reward draw that grew with every friend invited, so the page spread itself.

nodes.ua-creative-strategy.sections.1.it.text: Owned the testing framework: Translated acquisition goals into market-specific creative hypotheses, using performance data to steer tests across hooks, creative angles, scripts and formats.

Built the Creative Intelligence Dashboard: Used AI coding tools to build a dashboard that automates creative tagging and performance analysis, surfaces winning patterns and turns them into reusable scripts and playbooks.
Strengthened creator sourcing: Expanded regional talent pools through agency pitches and rotation, matching creators to the formats they perform best in.
Directed creator production: Briefed creators, developed script templates and reviewed every video before launch.

nodes.ua-creative-strategy.results.added.text: brand creative share of paid spend

nodes.zzz-jp-accounts.sections.0.items.a.text: The brief was to launch Zenless Zone Zero’s Japanese channels and hand them over once they could run on their own. With little precedent for channels like these in Japan, I had to learn the market while testing what worked, then turn scattered experiments into a system another team could run, all on a fixed timeline.

nodes.zzz-jp-accounts.sections.1.items.a.text: Defined the channel strategy: Mapped Japanese player behaviour, competitor channels and content gaps to give each channel a niche with proven demand and clear content pillars across YouTube and X.
Ran biweekly growth reviews: Tracked every channel against its KPIs, diagnosed the ones falling behind and brought winning formats from other niches to stalled channels to restart growth.
Managed agency partners: Coordinated three agencies, aligning briefs, reviews and performance targets to lift content quality and cost efficiency.
Handed over a repeatable system: Codified content learnings, KPIs and routines into playbooks, and transferred all nine channels to the Zenless Zone Zero team.

nodes.zzz-jp-accounts.results.added-21cb.text: channels hitting view targets at handover

nodes.gip-testing.sections.0.items.added.text: Genshin Impact’s paid acquisition relied mainly on brand creative. TikTok’s UGC incentive programme opened up a new possibility: could it bring in users efficiently as a channel, and could its videos work as ad creative? I needed to design a testing framework to find out.

nodes.gip-testing.sections.1.items.added.text: Designed the test framework: Built a three-round roadmap, setting each round’s payout model (CPM or CPA), markets, themes, budgets and success metrics against our acquisition benchmarks.
Led campaign execution: Owned all three rounds end to end, from task setup and creator briefs to progress tracking, submission reviews and recaps.
Evaluated the channel and drove the decision: Measured reach, CPI, user quality and content relevance, then recommended stopping the programme and shifting budget to creator ads.

nodes.gip-testing.results.added-c2840424.text: lower CPM in Round 3 than Round 1

nodes.xbox-launch.sections.0.items.added.text: The launch needed paid media to drive traffic to the Xbox landing page, not just awareness. That meant turning existing brand materials into 100+ localised assets, our team’s largest creative test for a paid brand campaign, with tight coordination across languages, platform specs and approvals.

nodes.xbox-launch.sections.1.items.added.text: Defined the creative strategy: Used past campaign learnings and regional player insights to build four testable creative concepts, then localised them into US, French and German versions to see which won in each market.

Partnered on media optimisation: Shaped budget, regional priorities and targeting with the media strategist across YouTube, Meta, X and TikTok, then reviewed live results together to scale winners and pause underperformers.
Managed creative production: Wrote briefs covering copy, landing-page links and platform specs for all 144 assets, and kept timelines, reviews and approvals on track.

nodes.influencer-activation.sections.0.i.text: Engagement on Genshin Impact’s recurring character campaigns on X was flattening, and it was weakest among English-speaking players. Our previous creator campaign aimed for broad appeal: many of its creators reached general gaming audiences rather than core Genshin players, so it brought reach but under 3% engagement.
This time, I needed a creator lineup built around core players that would drive them to the official event on X and its in-game reward codes.

nodes.influencer-activation.sections.1.i.text: Set the creator strategy: Built the lineup around the artists, cosplayers, streamers and Genshin news creators that core players follow, so 80% of creators reached core players rather than general gaming audiences.
Localised for English-speaking players: Made English-language creators half the lineup and briefed a US agency on the art styles local players respond to.
Owned the full creator lifecycle: Ran budget, sourcing, briefing, timelines and approvals across two agencies, then benchmarked results to decide what to scale next.

nodes.giveaway-campaign.sections.1.items.text: Designed the campaign: Partnered with the fan account (1M+ followers). To enter, players quote-posted the giveaway with their own creative take, and in-game reward codes turned views into a measurable action.
Activated creators across platforms: Coordinated 67 creators across X, TikTok and Instagram, who posted their own entries first to show players how to join.

Led execution and the recap: Aligned four agencies on briefs, content review, timelines and tracking. Codes beat the goal, but fewer players entered because quote-posting a creative entry took too much effort. The lesson: fan-account giveaways need one-tap actions, like a repost or a reply.

nodes.genshin-en-accounts.sections.0.ite.text: Genshin Impact ran English-language social channels on TikTok and YouTube to keep players engaged between major updates. The established channels had stalled: formats were getting repetitive, fewer viewers were following and views dropped between updates. New channels needed a strategy built from scratch, all while keeping CPM under target.

nodes.genshin-en-accounts.sections.1.ite.text: Diagnosed what stalled growth: Benchmarked each channel against TikTok trends and competitors, and pinpointed the gaps: too few evergreen topics, stale formats, weak follower conversion.
Refreshed the content mix: Moved guide channels from content that only worked on update days to evergreen gameplay tips, so views held up between updates.
Built strategy for the new channels: Set audience, positioning, content pillars and cadence for each, then refined them on early data before scaling.
Ran monthly reviews: Tracked KPIs and kept the agency’s output on each channel’s growth goals.

nodes.interactive-filter.sections.0.item.text: Lantern Rite needed a social moment players could join, and this year the filter challenge was moving beyond TikTok to Snapchat for the first time. The filters had to be fun to use, simple enough for anyone to recreate, and right for two different platforms. We also had only a short window to build momentum and get the trend to take off.

nodes.interactive-filter.sections.1.item.text: Shaped the filter concepts: Researched competitor filters and co-developed two gesture-based ideas: releasing a sky lantern for TikTok and Snapchat, and a lion-mask transformation for a new character on TikTok. I wrote the creative briefs and reviewed each iteration with TikTok’s effects team.
Briefed creators: Turned each filter into simple video ideas for cosplay, beauty, pet, dance and transition creators, so their posts inspired players to make their own.
Vetted creators and content: Reviewed creator selection and videos for 70+ creators across TikTok and Snapchat, whose posts went live in the first week to kick off the trend.

nodes.landing-page.sections.1.items.adde.text: Benchmarked formats: Studied interactive web campaigns to find a mechanic with shareability built in.
Designed the hook: Chose a personality quiz, a proven viral format, so every player got a personalised result worth sharing, and kept it to three questions to cut drop-off.
Built the viral loop: Tied rewards to referrals. Finishing the quiz unlocked a reward draw and each friend invited earned another, so every share brought in about 4 new visitors.

nodes.landing-page.results.added-67b3312.text: players in the draw, +60% vs benchmark

nodes.ai-workbench.sections.0.items.2.en.text: Script Studio: Turns the winning formula into new scripts, written natively for each market.

nodes.ai-workbench.sections.0.items.3.en.text: Campaign planning: Drafts the creative plan for the next campaign from past results.

nodes.ai-workbench.headline.note.en.text: I built it from scratch while running creative strategy for Genshin Impact's creator ads.

nodes.xhs-ai-channel.sections.0.items.0..text: Positioning: Studied the top AI creators and aimed the channel at AI beginners, with one promise: every video ends with something viewers can make themselves.

nodes.xhs-ai-channel.sections.0.items.1..text: Content formula: Found what makes people save and follow, and built every video around it: result first, low barrier, clear steps.

nodes.xhs-ai-channel.sections.0.items.2..text: Test and scale: Kept testing new formats and topics, cut what didn’t convert, and doubled down on what worked.

nodes.xhs-ai-channel.sections.0.items.3..text: Brand partnerships: Won paid partnerships with China’s leading AI companies, including Alibaba’s Qwen, ByteDance’s Jimeng, MiniMax, Moonshot AI’s Kimi, LiblibAI and Lovart.

nodes.xhs-ai-channel.sections.0.items.4..text: Content operations system: Built my own AI system for research, scripts and performance reviews, so I can run the whole channel on my own.

nodes.creator-workbench.sections.0.items.text: Built on a proven workflow: Every module is a workflow I already run for my own channel, from research and viral-post breakdowns to scripts and growth reviews.
End to end: Takes content from research to idea, script, review and post-launch analysis in one place, instead of across chats, docs and spreadsheets.
Human in the loop: Agents research, analyse and draft, but nothing gets made until the creator picks the idea, and every draft stops for review.
Built for other creators: Helps new users set up their own content tags from a few sample posts, runs on the AI subscription they already pay for, and works in Chinese and English.

nodes.xhs-ai-channel.summary.en.text: I built a channel from zero on Xiaohongshu (RedNote) and Douyin that shows beginners what they can make with AI tools, and run it like a growth project: find the audience, test what works, scale it, and turn the reach into paid partnerships with China’s leading AI companies.

nodes.seminary-coop.sections.0.items.0.e.text: Ran the social calendar: Planned and published posts, stories and carousels across Instagram, X and Facebook, and used performance data to refine what went out.

nodes.seminary-coop.sections.0.items.1.e.text: Coordinated the Summer Gift Guide: Brought the campaign together across the website, social and newsletters.

nodes.nike.sections.0.items.0.en.text: Supported launch campaigns: Helped run the Xiaohongshu (RedNote) campaigns that built awareness for Nike Women’s product launches.

nodes.nike.sections.0.items.1.en.text: Hashtag and influencer strategy: Developed the #NikeOOTD hashtag and optimised the influencer and UGC programmes, adding 1.33M+ hashtag views month on month.

nodes.nike.sections.0.items.2.en.text: Competitor research: Turned competitor analysis into changes to Nike’s account strategy, SEO and paid search, growing followers by 16K+ (45% year on year) and engagement by 173%.

nodes.weber-shandwick.sections.0.items.0.text: Research and social listening: Fed desk research, soundbite analysis and social listening into PR strategy and media sourcing for GUESS, Bosideng and Mido, and wrote the slogan for the GUESS × CLOTTEE campaign.

nodes.weber-shandwick.sections.0.items.1.text: Launch support: Drafted press releases and supported media outreach for GUESS’s Disney collection launch, helping lift GUESS’s Q3 PR value by 33%.

nodes.nowness.sections.0.items.0.en.text: Ran the accounts: Managed publishing on WeChat and Weibo, optimising content and timing for impressions and engagement.

nodes.nowness.sections.0.items.1.en.text: Content and layout: Helped shape and lay out art and culture pieces, contributing to 10K+ new followers and a 15% rise in read-through.

nodes.xjtlu.sections.0.items.1.en.text: Final-year research: How a Chinese rap show defined “authentic” hip-hop for its audience, using discourse and content analysis of lyrics and viewer reviews.
